gaps.sentence: I ___ exactly what you mean, so there is no need to explain again.
gaps.explanation: 'Understand' is a state verb and is not used in continuous forms, so the present simple is correct.

gaps.sentence: He ___ in the garden when the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress interrupted by a short event — past continuous.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: I can't talk now — I ___ dinner for twelve people.
gaps.hint: now plus a temporary activity in progress
gaps.explanation: 'Now' marks a temporary action in progress, so the present continuous is needed: am cooking.

gaps.sentence: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
gaps.hint: a timeless scientific fact takes present simple
gaps.explanation: General truths and scientific facts take the present simple: boils.

gaps.sentence: I ___ that film three times, and I would happily watch it again.
gaps.hint: life experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Experience up to the present with no specific past time takes the present perfect: have seen.

gaps.sentence: The moon ___ round the Earth roughly every 27 days.
gaps.hint: a timeless fact about the moon
gaps.explanation: Timeless facts take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: When you ___ John tomorrow, please give him my regards.
gaps.hint: no will after when for the future
gaps.explanation: In time clauses referring to the future, English uses the present simple, not 'will': see.
